opId.description: A unique ID for this call. Reuse it only when retrying the same call.

summary.description: Your plan, or your findings as numbered notes.

verdict.description: Required for plan_review, review and QA steps; null for a plan step.

watchpointNotes.description: Review and QA steps only: one entry per watchpoint file you checked, { path, note } with the note starting ✓ when it holds up or ⚠ when it does not, and why, at most 400 characters. Leave it out of a plan or plan review.

followUps.description: Review, plan review and QA steps only: real problems that should not reject the work (on a later round, ones that are new and not caused by the fix). 10db files each as a task in the Icebox column and names it in your result.

title.description: The outcome, as what is true when it is done.

description.description: What you saw, where, and why it matters.

builderCalls.description: Plan and plan review steps only. The builder alone owns seven things: money (owns money), a move with no undo (one_way_door), the agent's guardrails: the git guard, Codex rules, sandbox profiles, judge policy, trust grants, standing approvals, .mcp.json, hooks and CI workflows (guardrails), what the product does or how it looks and what done means (product_and_taste), a promise in the builder's name such as a release or a first message to someone (promise), a sign-in, credential or host command only a person can give (your_hands), and a spent budget (out_of_moves). A plan step always sends this: one { owns, call } per decision its brief needs from the builder, or [] when it needs nothing, so the build can start without waiting. A plan review always sends it too: the calls the plan makes that its brief does not declare, or [] when there are none. A plan review that leaves it out sends the plan to the builder.
